rows.figure: For every child who dies from drowning, another five receive emergency department (ED) care for their submersion injuries
rows.scope: United States; children (the paragraph's preceding sentence refers to children 14 and younger; the ratio sentence itself names no age band); emergency-department visits for nonfatal submersion injuries per child drowning death. The same paragraph states its death average 'from 2005 through 2014'; the ratio sentence carries no separate year range. This is the 2016-onward wording of CDC's 'Unintentional Drowning: Get the Facts' sheet; the 24 October 2014 version was not opened.
rows.source: CDC, 'Unintentional Drowning: Get the Facts' fact sheet (cited as 'Home and Recreational Safety Water Injury Fact Sheet'), restated verbatim on CDC's NSSP page 'Drowning and Submersion Syndrome Definitions' (last updated 23 April 2024, last reviewed 13 January 2026), reference 1
rows.do_not_add_to: Children only, United States only, emergency-department denominator only. A ratio, not a count: do not multiply into death totals, and do not combine with the 2022 CDC 'seven' ratio (row cdc-children-nonfatal-ed-7), with all-ages ratios, or with other countries' ratios.
rows.note: The 24 October 2014 page cited by BMJ Open 2015;5:e008444 (reference 2) could not be opened: every web archive was blocked, rate-limited or JavaScript-gated (see tried). Contemporaneous quotations of the same sheet pair 'another five' with 'from 2005-2009' and 3,533 deaths a year (June 2012 and July 2014), so the 2014 version most likely covered 2005-2009, but that is unverified. CDC's 2022 Drowning Facts document says seven for children under 18. Found by an independent agent, 21 Oct 2026.

notes: What was found. (1) The exact CDC page the papers cite is 'Unintentional drowning: get the facts', dated 24 October 2014 in BMJ Open 2015;5:e008444 reference 2 (read on PMC), at http://www.cdc.gov/homeandrecreationalsafety/water-safety/waterinjuries-factsheet.html; the page itself could not be opened on any host (see tried), so acceptance checks 1 and 2 (a quote from the archived page with its capture date, and the data years as that page states them) are NOT met and the status is partial. (2) The sentence survives in CDC's own words on a live CDC page: the NSSP 'Drowning and Submersion Syndrome Definitions' page (last updated 23 April 2024, reviewed 13 January 2026) restates the fact sheet as 'For every child who dies from drowning, another five receive emergency department (ED) care for their submersion injuries' in a paragraph whose death average is 'from 2005 through 2014', citing the fact sheet as reference 1. That is the row returned, graded A because the producing organisation is CDC, but a reviewer may prefer to hold it at C until the archived 2014 page is read, because it is a restatement on a later CDC page rather than the fact sheet itself. Note the NSSP wording says 'for their submersion injuries' where the fact sheet and its reposts say 'for nonfatal submersion injuries'. (3) Data years by version, from dated quotations of the sheet: June 2012 (MySafe:LA) and 7 July 2014 (USLA) pair the sheet with 'from 2005-2009' and 3,533 deaths a year; June 2016 (Methodist), June 2017 (Children's Safety Network) and July 2017 (Patch) pair it with 'From 2005-2014' and 3,536. So the 24 October 2014 version almost certainly printed 2005-2009 and the 2005-2014 wording arrived with a 2016 revision, but no document dated between October 2014 and April 2016 was found to confirm it; the row's scope therefore states 2005 through 2014 as the only years a CDC page was seen to state, and flags the 2014 years as unverified. (4) The Internet Archive's availability API reports a capture of the page on 18 April 2023 (status 200), and emDocs accessed it on 8 October 2020, so the page lived from at least 2012 to 2023 and was retired before the 6 January 2025 restoredcdc.org snapshot. (5) Comparison row cdc-children-nonfatal-ed-7 (seven, children under 18, CDC Drowning Facts reviewed 7 October 2022) needs no correction; the two figures are different CDC statements from different data years and age bands (14 and younger in the older sheet's paragraph; under 18 in 2022) and must not be averaged or combined. (6) An all-ages CDC-derived ratio was seen in passing: N Engl J Med 2012;366:2102-2110 prints 'another four persons receive care in the emergency department for nonfatal drowning' citing CDC WISQARS 2009; proposed as a next task, not added here. For a person with a browser: open https://web.archive.org/web/2014*/http://www.cdc.gov/HomeandRecreationalSafety/Water-Safety/waterinjuries-factsheet.html (also try the all-lower-case path and https) and choose a capture dated late October to December 2014; the footer should read 'Page last updated: October 24, 2014'. Under the heading 'How big is the problem?' quote the bullet beginning 'From 2005-' (expected '2005-2009 ... 3,533 ... about ten deaths per day') and the bullet 'For every child who dies from drowning, another five receive emergency department care for nonfatal submersion injuries', with its footnote number and the reference it points to (expected: CDC WISQARS). Then open a capture from mid-2016 to confirm when the years changed to 2005-2014, and one from 2021-2023 to see whether 'five' had become 'seven' before the page was retired. Archive-It (wayback.archive-it.org/all/) and archive.cdc.gov may also show it in a browser; both are JavaScript-gated here.
